mode_config.tooling: built-in WebSearch + WebFetch only (no Exa/Firecrawl/other providers)

query_verbatim: research the va-cue-system product as a legitimately viable product to sell on the market such that it earns a reasonably high income for me over the long term (150k minimum, 200k+ max). Ensure you investigate existing companies and products that would threaten its success and how I could beat them, work around them, or find a specific successful niche

monetization_models_in_scope: per-seat SaaS to fee-charging VA-accredited agents/attorneys
done-for-you per-file CUE/effective-date reviews sold to firms (B2B)
API / white-label licensing to existing VA tools, VSOs, county/state veterans offices
hybrids; recommend the most effective model
monetization_models_excluded: founder-run accredited practice (founder will not seek accreditation)
user_constraints_from_clarification.capacity: solo founder, full-time, bootstrapped (no outside capital)
user_constraints_from_clarification.income_definition: pre-tax owner earnings after business costs
user_constraints_from_clarification.accreditation: founder NOT planning to become VA-accredited
user_constraints_from_clarification.adjacent_pivots: IN SCOPE (user added after plan review): adjacent markets outside VA (e.g., SSDI, ERISA/LTD, military records correction/discharge upgrades, federal disability retirement, workers' comp) and adjacent VA niches

decision_informed: Whether to commit 2-3 years of solo full-time effort to the VA Effective-Date & CUE Engine, and if so with which monetization model and niche beachhead; or which adjacent pivot is stronger.
audience: The founder (solo technical founder, USAF veteran, ~10 yrs SWE incl. agentic AI/Graph RAG; develops via Claude Code).

in_scope: Competitor landscape as of Oct 2026 (VA-claims AI tools, legal-AI incumbents, VA/disability case-management software, SSDI-practice AI)
Customer pain, frequency, and willingness to pay for CUE / earliest-effective-date work
Current fee-eligible population and VA fee pool (re-verify July 2026 figures)
Monetization models, price benchmarks, and their legality for a non-accredited vendor
The data moat (commercial availability of historical point-in-time CFR; BVA/CAVC corpora)
Distribution channels, CAC drivers, and regulatory/policy durability risks
Adjacent pivots that reuse the same core asset (retroactive-error detection over a chronology + point-in-time law)
An income model translating revenue to owner earnings (founder-facing modeling on verified inputs; labeled as such)
excluded: Re-establishing technical feasibility (settled in July 2026 passes) except where facts may have changed
Selling directly to VA (B2G) as the primary model (locked out by prior strategy; mentioned only if evidence forces it)
Consumer (veteran-paying) model for claim assistance (regulatory risk; mentioned only as a competitor segment)
Legal advice: regulatory interpretation is flagged for counsel

working_numbers_to_refine.implied_revenue_target_initial_guess: ~$200K-$350K/yr, refined in the income model with sourced cost inputs

angles.A: VA-claims AI competitor sweep as of Oct 2026
angles.B: Legal-AI incumbents + VA/disability case-management + SSDI-practice AI + medical-record-review AI
angles.C: Demand, pain & market size (CUE/effective-date frequency & value, OIG error findings, accredited counts, fee pool, small-firm AI adoption & tech spend)
angles.D: Monetization benchmarks + legality for a non-accredited B2B vendor
angles.E: Moat/data: commercial historical point-in-time CFR/USC; BVA/CAVC/Fed Cir corpora
angles.G: Adjacent pivots outside VA (SSDI, ERISA LTD, federal disability retirement/OWCP, workers' comp)
angles.H: Unit-economics cost inputs (OCR/LLM cost, insurance, SOC 2, payments, SMB SaaS churn/CAC benchmarks)
angles.I: Military/VA-adjacent niches (discharge upgrades/BCMR/DRB, DES medical retirement & class settlements, CRSC/CRDP, DIC/accrued, SMC, PACT/Nehmer retro, VA overpayment debt)
